## Highlights

- Running and sliding windows over historical VaR, CVaR, trimmed and winsorized means, weighted quantiles and drawdown-at-risk now cost O(log n) per row instead of rescanning the frame. A running trimmed mean over one million rows completes in under one second, where it previously took several minutes. [#110](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/110)
- Twenty-two SQL-macro aggregates, including `fin_tracking_error`, `fin_hit_ratio`, `fin_realized_vol`, `fin_parkinson_vol` and `fin_stable_cov`, can be used as window functions with `OVER (...)`. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- The return and risk SQL macros validate `annualization`, rate and threshold arguments in the same way as the native functions. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)

## Upgrading from 0.3.1

0.3.2 is a patch release for DuckDB v2.0.0. Version constraints that select the 0.3 line pick it up. It does not change any function signature, but several macros now raise an error for arguments that previously produced a numeric result.

1. Update the extension with `FORCE INSTALL finance FROM community;` (or `UPDATE EXTENSIONS (finance);`), then `LOAD finance;`.
2. Search existing SQL for the macros listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility) and confirm that every `annualization` argument is positive and every rate or threshold argument is finite and greater than -1.
3. Re-run reports that use `fin_stable_corr` or `fin_realized_corr` on series that can be constant, and handle the NULL result where `NaN` was expected before.

Changes to check:
- [Argument validation in return and risk macros](#compatibility)
- [NULL results for constant series and overflow](#compatibility)

## Features

- The following SQL-macro aggregates run as window functions, and a framed value equals the grouped result over the rows of the frame: `fin_kahan_sum`, `fin_stable_mean`, `fin_stable_cov`, `fin_stable_corr`, `fin_realized_cov`, `fin_realized_corr`, `fin_weighted_stddev`, `fin_arithmetic_return`, `fin_expectancy`, `fin_upside_deviation`, `fin_semivariance`, `fin_tracking_error`, `fin_active_return`, `fin_hit_ratio`, `fin_win_rate`, `fin_loss_rate`, `fin_realized_variance`, `fin_realized_vol`, `fin_vol_of_vol`, `fin_parkinson_vol`, `fin_garman_klass_vol` and `fin_rogers_satchell_vol`. Previously DuckDB rejected these calls with a binder error. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- Historical `fin_var` and `fin_cvar`, `fin_trimmed_mean`, `fin_winsorized_mean` and `fin_weighted_quantile` (default `linear` method) rank each partition once and update each frame incrementally. `fin_drawdown_at_risk` and `fin_conditional_drawdown_at_risk` use the same index for frames that start at the first row of the partition. Results are unchanged. Per-row configuration, parametric and Cornish-Fisher VaR, and discrete weighted-quantile methods continue to use frame-by-frame evaluation. [#110](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/110)
- NYSE business-day functions read a holiday table precomputed for 1900 to 2199, which makes `fin_is_business_day` and `fin_next_business_day` three to four times faster on that range. Dates outside the range use the calendar rules as before. [#110](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/110)
- `fin_mann_whitney_u` is faster on large samples. The statistic and p-value are unchanged. [#110](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/110)

## Bug Fixes

- `fin_upside_deviation`, `fin_semivariance` and `fin_hit_ratio` returned `0.0` when the threshold argument was NULL. They now return NULL. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- Return and risk macros returned `0.0`, `NaN` or a negative variance when `annualization` was zero, negative or non-finite, for example `fin_realized_variance(r, -1)`, `fin_tracking_error(r, b, 0)` and `fin_cagr(r, 0)`. They now raise the error that the function reference documents, such as `fin_semivariance: annualization must be positive and finite`. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- Macros that take an annual rate, minimum acceptable return or threshold accepted values that are non-finite or not greater than -1 and produced meaningless results. They now raise an error. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)

## Compatibility

- The following macros raise an error for a non-positive or non-finite `annualization` argument, and, where the macro takes one, for a rate, minimum acceptable return or threshold that is non-finite or not greater than -1: `fin_upside_deviation`, `fin_semivariance`, `fin_hit_ratio`, `fin_realized_variance`, `fin_realized_vol`, `fin_tracking_error`, `fin_cagr`, `fin_omega_ratio`, `fin_information_ratio`, `fin_alpha`, `fin_treynor_ratio` and `fin_realized_quarticity`. Queries that passed such values and used the numeric result must correct the arguments. A NULL rate or threshold returns NULL. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- `fin_stable_corr` and `fin_realized_corr` return NULL for a constant series instead of `NaN`, which matches `fin_beta`. In the macros that now run as window functions, a result that overflows to infinity is returned as NULL. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)

## Maintenance

- The documentation describes how to serve `finance` to DuckDB 2.0 clients over the Quack remote protocol, and which client queries require the extension to be loaded on the client. The community install smoke workflow also tests a Quack server. [#109](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/109)
- Six macro definitions that were never registered were removed from the source. A duplicate macro name now fails when the extension loads. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- The outdated 0.2 roadmap page was removed from the documentation site, and earlier sweep reports and benchmark data moved to `history/`. `make covariance-example` no longer requires a writable DuckDB build directory. [#111](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/111)
- Source, community manifest and package metadata are aligned at 0.3.2.
